item.title: Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan loss confidence vote in parliament after largest party, PSD, quit his
item.description: Romania's Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan lost a confidence vote after the Social Democrats quit his coalition. Lawmakers voted him out of office due to unpopular austerity measures. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan has been voted out of office by lawmakers.

item.description: Modi's BJP won the key state of West Bengal for the first time. But the vote has thrown up questions that won't go away. What Modi’s big win in Indian state elections could mean for its democracy.

item.title: Sudan's military accuses Ethiopia, UAE of drone attacks, recalls its ambassador
item.description: Sudan recalled its ambassador and accused Ethiopia and the UAE of drone attacks. A Military Spokesperson in Sudan said the government has evidence that four drone strikes that have happened since March 1 came from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport.

item.title: U.S. and Iran exchange taunts as attacks imperil fragile ceasefire
item.description: Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf region threatened a fragile US-Iran ceasefire. The incidents raised concerns about the ceasefire's stability, with the UAE reporting Iranian missile and drone strikes.

item.title: Ceasefire tested as Iran warns US the fight over Strait of Hormuz hasn’t ‘begun yet’
item.description: Iran warned the US the fight over Strait of Hormuz hasn’t begun yet. Live updates: Ceasefire tested as Iran warns US the fight over Strait of Hormuz hasn’t ‘begun yet’ CNN.

item.title: Two killed and many injured after car driven into crowd in German city of Leipzig
item.description: A car driven into a crowd in Leipzig killed two people. A 33-year-old German citizen was detained following the incident, the authorities say. Two killed and many injured after car driven into crowd in German city of Leipzig.

item.title: Thailand scraps 25-year-old agreement with Cambodia on joint energy exploration
item.description: Thailand scrapped a 25-year-old energy exploration agreement with Cambodia. The withdrawal was an election campaign pledge of Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, who earlier this year rode a wave of nationalism stoked by fierce fighting with Cambodia to become the first Thai premier to be reelected in two decades.

item.title: Beijing courts Europe amid US dysfunction
item.description: China is seeking new European allies as the US-Europe partnership falters. Beijing aims to secure a multipolar world order, with China playing a key role. China is hoping to secure new allies for a future multipolar world order as the partnership between the US and the European powers slides into a crisis.

item.title: Taiwan player victim of ‘inappropriate contact’ at UK table tennis event
item.description: A female Taiwanese table tennis player was subjected to inappropriate physical contact during a security check at a UK event. Officials are investigating the incident. Officials say a female player was subjected to inappropriate physical contact during a security check.

item.title: Car importer gets jail, S$1 million fine for under-declaring values of vehicles including Porsche
item.description: A Singaporean car importer was sentenced to jail and fined S$1 million for under-declaring vehicle values, including a Porsche 718 Cayman Style Edition. Customs launched an investigation after suspicious documents were submitted.

item.title: Rapper Kid Cudi removes British star M.I.A. from tour
item.description: US rapper Kid Cudi removed British singer M. I. A. from his tour, Rebels Rage, due to a disagreement between the two artists. M. I. A. was scheduled to be the opening act. British singer songwriter M. I. A will no longer be the opening act for Rebels Rage tour after disagreement with US rapper Kid Cudi.

item.title: Canadian prime minister says Europe will anchor world order
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told European leaders they will anchor the world order in the future, not the US. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney tells European leaders they, not the U. S., will anchor the world order in the future.

item.description: A cruise ship has 2 confirmed and 5 suspected hantavirus cases on board. A suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard an Atlantic cruise ship has triggered global concern. 2 Confirmed, 5 Suspected Cases On Board, Experts Warn There Is No Cure.

item.title: Singapore passes law to deal with incidents on cross border RTS Link
item.description: Singapore passed a law to handle incidents on the cross border RTS Link. The Bill that was passed on Tuesday will also allow Malaysia’s border laws to apply to designated areas of Singapore's RTS Link station.

item.title: Austrian Watchdog Files Complaint Against LinkedIn Over Paid Profile Views
item.description: Austria's watchdog filed a complaint against LinkedIn over paid profile views. Noyb said it was demanding LinkedIn be fined. (Representational). Austrian Watchdog Files Complaint Against LinkedIn Over Paid Profile Views.

item.title: U.S. attempt to open Strait of Hormuz tests fragile Iran war ceasefire
item.description: US forces attempted to open the Strait of Hormuz, testing a fragile Iran war ceasefire. The move came despite a reported ceasefire, with the UAE saying Iran fired missiles and drones at it, though the ceasefire seemed to be holding.
